summary: the largest time step for which a particle's root mean squared displacement in one step stays a stated fraction of the smallest size

inputs.name: fraction
inputs.meaning: the largest root mean squared displacement in one step, as a fraction of the size

inputs.name: size
inputs.meaning: the smallest size in the system, the smallest particle's diameter for one

inputs.name: diffusivity
inputs.meaning: the largest diffusivity in the system, that of the smallest particle for one

inputs.name: dimensions
inputs.meaning: how many dimensions the particles move in

outputs.name: time_step_max
outputs.meaning: (fraction x size)^2 over 2 x dimensions x diffusivity

validity: a stochastic integration of diffusion, Brownian or Langevin, whose accuracy is set by the displacement per step; it is not the stability limit of a grid

source.citation: F. A. Oliveira, R. M. S. Ferreira, L. C. Lapas, M. H. Vainstein, Anomalous Diffusion: A Basic Mechanism for the Evolution of Inhomogeneous Systems, Front. Phys. 7 (2019) 18, doi:10.3389/fphy.2019.00018 (a review, open access) (read 2026-11-17, https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphy.2019.00018/pdf; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-oliveira-2019-anomalous-diffusion); A. Einstein, On the movement of small particles suspended in stationary liquids required by the molecular-kinetic theory of heat, Ann. Phys. 17 (1905) 549; read in the English translation of A. D. Cowper, in Investigations on the Theory of the Brownian Movement, ed. R. Fürth (Dover, 1956) (read 2026-11-17, https://archive.org/stream/brownian-motion-einstein/Brownian-Motion-Einstein_djvu.txt; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-einstein-1905-brownian-movement)
source.locus: Sec. 1.1, Eq. (1): the mean square displacement is 2dDt, d the spatial dimension, after Einstein; Secs. 4 and 5: the root of the mean squared displacement along one coordinate is sqrt(2Dt)
